 Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr.’s Injury Status Not Contract-Related
 By Sam Robinson |
 at October 18, 2026 4:54 pm 
 Joey Porter Jr.  played in his Cowboys debut, suiting up days after a trade ended his de facto hold-in with the Steelers , but the contract-year cornerback did not play in Week 5. An illness kept Porter on the sideline against the Buccaneers.
 A separate issue has Porter questionable heading into tonight’s Dallas-Green Bay matchup. Porter is dealing with an ankle injury suffered in practice this week, WFAA’s Ed Werder tweets . Porter logged two limited practices and a full practice, though the second limited session coming Friday calls his availability for Week 6 into question.
 Porter running into yet another issue naturally invites speculation about his pursuit of an extension. Contract structure drove his push out of Pittsburgh, with a back injury — a la Jalen Ramsey ’s 2019 effort to be traded out of Jacksonville — used as cover during that saga.
 Porter was on the Steelers’ 53-man roster from Weeks 1-4 but was ruled out each week. A move from full practices (walkthroughs, as the Steelers were preparing for a Thursday-night game in Porter’s final days with the team) to a limited session in Week 4 provided the last straw for Pittsburgh , and it is fair to wonder if these two new health developments are contract-related as well.
 While Porter’s health issues invite suspicion, Werder adds this latest update has nothing to do with his contract. Porter hopes to play tonight. The 26-year-old corner is due for free agency — barring an extension or a franchise tag — in March. The Cowboys are interested in keeping the high-priced trade pickup long term , and Porter said following the swap he hopes to finish his career in Dallas . He and fellow ex-Steelers second-round pick George Pickens both reside as 2027 tag candidates, giving the Cowboys a ticking clock.
 The Cowboys do not share the Steelers’ long-held apprehension toward guarantees past Year 1 of contracts, putting Porter in position to score a modern second contract. A $28MM-per-year Pittsburgh offer looked to come with the organization’s built-in guardrails regarding future guarantees, helping lead Porter to seek an exit ramp. Like Pickens, Porter agreed to suit up on his rookie deal and allow his team team evaluation time. But the second-generation NFL defender is not off to a good start with the Cowboys.
 Exaggerating health concerns with two different teams would obviously make Porter a shaky long-term bet for the Cowboys, and the fact that he played against the Texans two weeks ago does make these recent health setbacks appear coincidental when connected to his contract status. But the fourth-year veteran will need to begin impressing on the field in Dallas soon if he wants to submit a strong case for a big-ticket second contract.
